events.title: Intel 8086 introduced
events.summary: Intel introduced the 8086 [microprocessor] in June 1978 — a 16-bit [CPU] that became the foundation of the x86 architecture.
events.about: The 8086 and its cost-reduced 8088 variant powered the [IBM] [PC] and every compatible clone — the ISA developers still target today in compatibility mode. Segmented addressing and the instruction set defined [PC] software for decades. From [DOS] to Windows to Linux on x86 servers, the lineage starts here.

narrative.whyChosen: The 8086 established the x86 instruction set that still underpins most desktop and server CPUs.
narrative.whyImportant: [IBM] chose the 8088 for the [PC], making Intel's architecture the industry standard.
narrative.problemSolved: 8-bit CPUs could not address enough memory for growing business applications.
